title: Metroid: Samus Returns
subtitle: MercurySteam / Nintendo EPD · Nintendo 3DS

body: Metroid: Samus Returns is MercurySteam and Nintendo's Nintendo 3DS reimagining of Metroid II. Samus Aran descends into SR388 to eliminate the Metroids, searching a planet whose tunnels conceal different stages of the creatures' development. Equipment expands her movement and access as the hunt advances. The story follows the earlier Game Boy journey, but three-dimensional scenery, new rooms and revised encounters change its physical character. The side-view adventure gives Samus more precise control over her weapons and another answer to an enemy approaching at close range.

Samus can stand still and aim around a full circle, choosing the angle needed to reach an exposed target. The Melee Counter provides a different kind of precision: recognising the signal before a physical attack and responding at the right moment can stun the attacker. Both actions encourage attention to an enemy's position and behaviour. A fight becomes easier when the player identifies the opening, rather than merely firing into the space ahead while trying to avoid everything that enters it.

Aeion abilities draw on a separate energy supply. Scan Pulse reveals nearby map information and hidden passages, giving the player a means of investigating a promising but apparently closed area. Other abilities assist fighting or movement, while transport stations shorten return journeys through the growing map. MercurySteam developed the game under the supervision of longtime Metroid producer Yoshio Sakamoto. Its combination of counters, free aiming and side-view exploration preceded the studio's later work with Nintendo on Metroid Dread, which carried those ideas into a new mission.
story_headings: Aim freely, then answer a charge
